newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA TAKES IN 80 PCT OF WHEAT CROP, HAS LOSSES.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA TAKES IN 80 PCT OF WHEAT CROP, HAS LOSSES.

text.p: Romania has taken in 80 percent of its 1997 wheat crop and data show a good average yield but bad weather has seriously affected almost 200,000 ha under wheat, the Agriculture Ministry said on Tuesday.
Ministry data showed average yield on the 1.92 million ha harvested so far amounted to 3,065 kg per ha, up from initial estimates of 2,963 kg.
The total area under wheat was 2.38 million ha this year.
A ministry statement said heavy rains and floods over the past few weeks had damaged 196,924 ha under wheat and rye. It gave no breakdown for the two crops.

Reports in the local media in recent weeks said adverse weather had significantly delayed wheat harvesting, affecting the quality of the unharvested milling wheat or turning the crop on thousands of hectares into fodder.
Wheat in some areas had started to germinate due to high humidity and farmers had reportedly recorded heavy losses.
Farming ministry officials have been reluctant so far to comment on the impact of bad weather on the quality of the wheat harvested since heavy rains hit the country last month.
On Tuesday, the state news agency Rompres quoted ministry State Secretary Aurel Pana as saying bad weather had caused "significant losses".
"We are still evaluating the damaged areas. Data gathering is continuing. Under the present circumstances it would be a mistake to make an assessment now," he said.
Latest ministry estimates put the 1997 wheat crop at 6.9 million tonnes, compared with 3.1 million last year.
